purpose: Core entry points and build system for the SupplyMind OpenEnv environment: baseline.py (LLM agent calling an OpenAI-compatible endpoint against the in-process env), inference.py (competition-spec HTTP-client agent emitting [START]/[STEP]/[END] lines), scripted_agent.py (deterministic rule-based baseline), models.py (pydantic action/observation contract), openenv.yaml (env manifest), plus Dockerfile (main API), Dockerfile.dashboard (Streamlit), Dockerfile.damocles (v3 model-serving API), docker-compose.yml, Makefile, requirements*.txt, pyproject.toml.
verdict: Split personality. The Python entry-point half is genuinely real and works: I executed scripted_agent.py end-to-end (easy 0.7711, medium 0.6962, hard 0.6715) and a reset/step smoke test â€” no mock data, no canned LLM output, real retries, clean pydantic contract, valid manifest. The build-system half is bitrotted theater: the Damocles container cannot even start (uvicorn module path is stale from the phase4 versions/ rename â†’ ModuleNotFoundError crash loop), and even if it started, /rag and /forecast crash on a broken ROOT-relative path (resolves to versions/models/ which doesn't exist), /rl/act needs sb3 + a .zip checkpoint that the image deliberately excludes (it copies an .onnx the app never loads), and /assess hard-requires an Ollama daemon at 127.0.0.1:11434 that isn't in the image â€” so 4 of 5 advertised endpoints of that service are dead on arrival. docker-compose sets DEMO_MODE=true/OFFLINE_MODE=true on all three services but no production code reads either var â€” placebo switches whose stated intent ("no live API calls") also contradicts the everything-live mandate. The main Dockerfile's COPY . . plus a .dockerignore that ignores none of models/ (9.9 GB), versions/ (31.6 GB), or rl/ (0.9 GB) makes the "slim production image" a ~43 GB build in practice. Dockerfile.dashboard ships a dashboard whose own docstring says DEPRECATED. The Makefile promises 9 health probes but has 8, tags v4.0-final-submit on a v6.0 repo, and its benchmark target depends on local Ollama. pip install . is broken because pyproject's packages.find can never pick up top-level models.py/baseline.py that server.app imports. Two of three compose services are fake-alive at best.
